evidence: numerical-uncalibrated simulation re-run from a copy of sim/ plus literature/web checks; nothing built or flown; not a physical test
scripts: recheck.mjs (12 spot cases + footageStability; ALL=1 → all 39 cases with auditor metric code)
fs_all.mjs (shared footageStability on all 17 flown cases, near-miss gates)

fullEnsembleRerun.diffs: run_all.mjs re-run in a copy: all 39 ensemble rows, summary, byWind, sensitivities and dt table identical to dev/descentglider/results.json. Only difference: results.json scenarios.* show STALE ensemble constants (e.g. fullrun avail 29.25, jitterRms 24.0 FAIL, keMax 18.93, ensRange max 99.1) from an older ensemble.js; the regenerated ensemble.js (repo) gives 29.89 / 1.39 / 18.02 / 69.8. Reporting inconsistency only.

avail.note: auditor denominator = fullrun col.riding (dev: rider speed >2 m/s); −0.8 pt in flown cases. 22/39 runs are wind-interlock no-fly (all 6 m/s except tail6_s11/s12, all 9 m/s).

pxMed.note: not independently recomputed (analysis.js geometry reused); p10 304 px, min 134 px (tail6_s11). Conditional on 80° lens + 3-servo cradle.

jitterRms.note: dev jitter masks frames where the crop is clamped (lensOK≠1); the shared footageStability(R) does not and gives 18.1 °/s at p90 (tail3_s12) and 110 °/s (tail6_s11) — rider overtaking a close glider / losing it. Calm & cross-3 cases 1.1–1.4 °/s (pass). Pass only inside the calm/cross ≤3 m/s envelope.

addedMass.note: glider 124 g + heated sleeve 60 g + tag 12 g + 18.5 Wh bank 120 g

bodyForcePeak.note: no tether; sleeve/bank are static weight (excluded by definition); hand throw is a user action. Acceptable.

handsBusy.note: throw and pick-up only while stopped

setupTime.note: fails even in calm (33.4–35.1 s: draw 3 s + climb to ready cue ≈8 s + landing wait ≈12 s + side-step + 5 s stow). Flown-only p90 48.7 s. No-fly runs are charged ≈50 s (throw, interlock landing, 30 s walk) — a real user would not throw in 6–9 m/s, slightly disfavouring the concept but not changing the verdict.

ops.note: auditor adds +1 recovery action in no-fly runs where the glider never came to rest (head9_s11, crossR9_s12: dev already charges the 30 s recovery walk there but no action) → 6/39 runs with 3 actions = 15 % > 10 % → p90 = 3. Borderline: a 1-case change flips it.

keMax.note: tail6_s11: interlock did not trip (measured wind < 5.5 m/s), follow at 17.0 m/s ground speed → 18.0 J, 13 m from the body. Auditor body-segment distance (feet→head) instead of head distance changes nothing. Inside ≤3 m/s: max 13.7 J (pass, 1.2 J margin).

packVol.note: 35×12.5×6 cm folded sleeve (2.63 L) + bank 0.15 L; 66 cm span scissor-fold to 35 cm plausible but unbuilt

endurance.note: per-run accounting (flight energy throw→rest + 0.6 W heater over the whole 6 min lift; only riding minutes count as filming) gives 66.5 min — still ≥45. Flying cell 2 Wh → ≈9 runs at the mean, recharge 1.1–1.6 C on the lift needs a warm (>10 °C) cell, more than the 0.6 W heater budget is shown to deliver (unverified).

envelope.def: mean wind ≤3 m/s, all directions (dev text: calm–3 m/s, 9–13 m/s riders)
envelope.note: no envelope passes all judged metrics: setupTime fails in every wind bin (calm p90 35 s); 3 m/s tail wind avail 46–61 %; near-miss gates (head <1.5 m or landing <2.5 m) fail in 6/15 runs ≤3 m/s

massBudget.note: components.js: cam4k 16 + avionics 10 + 5 servos 12.5 + motorProp 11 + wiring 5 = 54.5 g shared items; explicit ASSUMED ToF 5 g, cradle 5 g, airframe 30 g, 2 Wh cell 13.3 g (150 Wh/kg) → 107.8 g ×1.15 = 124.0 g — arithmetic reproduced, <250 g (C0 mass OK). Airframe 30 g for a 0.065 m² folding wing with pod, hinge and spiked skid that must survive belly landings and 6–12 J snow strikes is optimistic; at 40 g airframe → 135.5 g, KE-cap speed 14.8 m/s; dev sensitivity +15 g → light-wind avail 75→65 %.

physics.assumption: Loiter at 40° bank ≈2.1 W drag power, ≈10.5 W electrical incl. 4.8 W avionics
physics.evidence: auditor hand check: W/S 18.7 N/m², n 1.31, CL 0.50, AR 6.7, e 0.85 → CD 0.064, D 0.20 N, P 2.0 W, R 12.0 m — reproduced. Propulsive 5.7 W electrical for 2.0 W drag implies η≈0.36: plausible for a 3.5″ prop at low thrust. Real micro wings (Flite Test 600 mm, 200 g AUW) fly 7–10 min on ≈6 Wh in sport flying (≈35–50 W) — not a cruise datum; no measured cruise datum for a 120 g wing found.
physics.killTest: wattmeter log of a 120–135 g, 0.065 m² wing orbiting at 40° bank, 10 m/s, −10 °C: electrical ≤12 W incl. avionics

physics.assumption: Hand throw at 10 m/s from the shoulder succeeds every time; pusher starts after 0.5 s ≥4.8 m from the helmet
physics.devClaim: deterministic throw, 0 launch failures in 39 cases
physics.evidence: hand-launched pusher wings are routine for hobbyists, but a gloved skier on skis at a slope top, throwing across/into gusty wind, is an untested population; tip-stall and pusher-prop hand strikes are known hand-launch failure modes. No failure rate is modelled.
physics.killTest: 50 throws by ≥5 gloved skiers standing on skis at 0–5 m/s wind: ≥95 % clean climb-out, 0 prop contacts

physics.assumption: Catch-up after a mid-run stop from the loiter
physics.devClaim: no catch-up at the top; after the mid-run stop ≈11 s to be within 10 m at 3 m/s
physics.evidence: reproduced in the run rows (catchUp[1] 7.7–17 s at 3 m/s); costs avail and is honestly counted. KE cap (14.7 m/s) leaves ≈1–1.7 m/s closing speed vs a 13 m/s rider.
physics.killTest: n/a (model consequence); flight test: time to station after restart ≤10 s in 3 m/s

physics.devClaim: up-slope wind gives slope lift, down-slope wind sinks
physics.evidence: reasonable first-order near-surface approximation on a uniform slope; ignores separation/lee rotors on convex terrain and tree edges. Not load-bearing: switching it off gives light-wind avail 77.6 vs 75.4 %.

physics.assumption: End-of-run belly landing ≈3.5 m beside the stopped rider at the lift approach, μk 0.35 spiked skid
physics.devClaim: landing point 3.5 m beside, slide 0–6 m
physics.evidence: ensemble: landMinRider <2.5 m in 4/17 flown runs (min 0.85 m, head3_s13), 2/12 runs at 3 m/s headwind end in a go-around followed by a snow strike (11–12 J); the lift approach is the most crowded place on the piste and other skiers are not modelled there.
physics.killTest: 30 autonomous landings beside a standing dummy in a roped area, 0–5 m/s: 100 % ≥2.5 m from the dummy, ≥90 % at rest within 8 m, 0 airframe damage

physics.assumption: Wind interlock 5.5 m/s + KE governor keep KE ≤14.9 J and range ≤50 m
physics.evidence: tail6_s11: measured wind stayed <5.5 m/s, glider followed at 17 m/s (18.0 J) and reached 69.8 m range with no fail-safe — both the KE governor and the 50 m geofence failed in the same run.
physics.killTest: software-in-the-loop: 100 tail-wind runs 4–7 m/s: KE ≤14.9 J and range ≤50 m in all

physics.devClaim: avail 75 % light wind vs 25.6 % without cradle
physics.evidence: eisRho 0.3 → jitter mean 2.72 °/s (still ≤3), avail 71 %; 2.5 g servos slewing 6 rad/s with a 16 g camera at −10 °C is unverified (cold servo torque/backlash).
physics.killTest: bench: cradle + camera on a rate table at −10 °C, residual after Gyroflow ≤10 % above 0.5 Hz

dominanceVsTowglider.claim: dominated by towglider except a no-line niche
dominanceVsTowglider.verdict: confirmed on the ensemble (setup, ops, KE, avail at ≥6 m/s). Exception beyond the no-line niche: in calm descentglider has higher avail (88 vs 72 %), at 3 m/s they tie — but it pays 33–35 s standstill and a landing near people every run, so towglider still dominates for a usable product. (Towglider numbers taken from dev/towglider/results.json, not re-audited here.)

findings.detail: tail6_s11: interlock not tripped, follow at 17 m/s → 18.0 J and 69.8 m range, no fail-safe event.

findings.detail: head3_s11/s12: go-around then snow strike at 11–12 J; tail6_s12: strike 13.6 s after the throw. Airframe survival of 30 g structure not modelled; a damaged glider ends the day.

findings.detail: subject 18.1 °/s p90, 110.6 °/s max (tail6_s11) vs dev masked jitter 1.39 °/s p90; calm/cross-3 cases 1.1–1.4 °/s.

findings.detail: fullrun scenario jitterRms 24.0 FAIL / avail 29.25 / ensRange 99.1 m vs regenerated ensemble.js 1.39 / 29.89 / 69.8.

findings.detail: +15 g already costs 10 pt avail; warm-cell charging needs more than shown.

safetyRegulatory: EU: 124 g (<250 g) can be C0-class; C0 follow-me must stay ≤50 m from the remote pilot (2019/945 Part 1) — breached once (69.8 m) in the ensemble; A1 follow-me height ≤50 m.
US: Part 107/recreational rules require VLOS by the operator or a visual observer; a skier facing downhill cannot watch a glider behind them — no legal US solo operation without a waiver.
Resort written permission (gate for every concept); many resorts ban drones outright.
Landing at the lift approach (the most crowded spot) every run; no bystander detection in the landing logic beyond the rider.
Pusher prop near the hand at throw; snow strikes at 6–12 J.
credibleEnvelope: calm to 3 m/s non-tail wind, groomed piste, 9–13 m/s riders: avail ≈81 % (recomputed), KE ≤13.7 J — but setupTime 33–49 s fails everywhere, and near-miss/landing-proximity events occur in that envelope. No envelope passes all judged metrics.
verdict: FAIL. Developer's self-assessment (fails; dominated by towglider) is honest and reproduced exactly; the audit adds ops p90 = 3, a footageStability fail and unjudged near-miss/geofence/crash events that make it worse. Not a usable solo follow-cam; keep only as a calm-day, no-line research niche.
